props.name: methanol synthesis catalyst (Australian methanol plant)
props.description: The catalyst of the methanol converter; the source names it only as 'a catalyst' and gives no composition, preparation or reduction.

props.name: austenitic steel against hydrogen attack
props.statement: 18/8 austenitic stainless steel is used in those parts of the ammonia and methanol converters subject to high temperature, for its resistance to hydrogen attack.

props.name: conversion up to 2 percent
props.statement: A conversion of up to 2% is obtained in the methanol converter; the methanol formed is condensed and contains approximately 20% water, and the unconverted gas is recirculated.

props.name: converter simpler than ammonia
props.statement: The methanol converter and circulation system are generally similar to but less elaborate than those used for ammonia synthesis; the gas passes through an interchanger with a by-pass, down through the catalyst and back through the interchanger.

props.name: crude methanol contains iron carbonyl
props.statement: The crude methanol from the synthesis plant contains up to 20% water and traces of iron carbonyl, ammonia and organic compounds; the iron carbonyl is removed by doping the crude spirit with 40% caustic and blowing with air for 24 hours.

props.name: feed composition set by ammonia plant
props.statement: The composition of the gas entering the methanol system is largely controlled by the requirements of the ammonia plant and the ability of the CO2 removal and CO removal plants to handle the corresponding gas rate.

props.name: interchanger failure mimics activity loss
props.statement: In the ammonia and methanol synthesis converters an interchanger failure is difficult to distinguish from loss of catalyst activity, since both result in reduced conversion and a lower exit-gas temperature; a gland or sheath failure causes a sudden loss of catalyst temperature.

props.name: liquid methanol cuts mild steel joints
props.statement: Liquid methanol under pressure will quickly cut the surface of a leaking mild-steel pipe joint; the pipe ends are therefore tipped with a welded deposit of hard alloy steel and stainless-steel lens rings are used for these joints.

props.name: little control of temperature gradient
props.statement: Very little control is obtainable over the temperature gradient through the methanol catalyst, and only by variation of the circulation rate; the inlet temperature of the gas going to the catalyst is controlled by adjusting the interchanger by-pass.

props.name: methanol converter failure easier to trace
props.statement: The cause of failure in a methanol converter is easier to trace than in an ammonia converter because of its simpler construction.

props.statement: The methanol synthesis reaction may be represented as CO + 2H2 = CH3OH with 24.6 kg cal liberated.

props.name: methanol unit ancillary to ammonia
props.statement: The methanol synthesis plant is run as an ancillary unit to the ammonia synthesis plant and normally would not operate unless the ammonia plant was synthesising ammonia; gas is piped from the compressor to the methanol circulation system and bled back to the inlet of the CO removal plant.

props.name: refined methanol specification
props.statement: With careful control of the continuous distillation it is possible to produce refined methanol meeting the stated specification, including methanol greater than 99%.

props.name: shift equilibrium versus rate
props.statement: As the iron-steam (shift) reaction is an exothermic equilibrium reaction, lower temperatures favour hydrogen production but reduce the reaction velocity considerably; to balance these, two catalyst beds of three trays with an intermediate interchanger are used.

props.name: synthesis pressure 350 ats
props.statement: The synthesis pressure of 350 ats on the Australian plants strikes an economic balance between the costs of compression, the size of plant and the conversion efficiencies obtained.

props.name: water scrubbing removes sulphur
props.statement: Countercurrent water scrubbing under pressure (125 lb/sq in gauge) removes the major portion of the CO2 and also removes organic sulphur compounds and some of the traces of H2S still in the gas.

props.name: gas returning from the CO2 removal plant (typical composition)
props.description: Gas after countercurrent water scrubbing at 125 lb/sq in gauge, returned to the 3rd compressor stage; from the 6th stage it goes to the CO removal plant or to the methanol synthesis plant.

props.description: Two beds of catalyst each of three trays with an intermediate interchanger removing heat from the partially converted gas; heat interchangers and countercurrent contact scrubbing (water heating tower) recover the reaction heat.

props.name: methanol converter (wall-cooled, 250 litre catalyst basket)
props.description: High-pressure converter in the same size forging as the ammonia converter, body hollow forged from chrome steel; internals of the wall-cooling type (incoming gas passes spirally down outside the basket), a coil-in-sheath stainless-steel interchanger at the base, a central pipe to a heater chamber with a 100 kW three-phase electric heater, then down through the catalyst bed and out through the hot side of the interchanger. Interchanger with by-pass; two temperature points in the catalyst bed. Operated in a gas circulation loop with condenser cooler, catchpots and a circulator. Dimension table (p. 62): inside diameter of the catalyst basket 1'3¼", length of the catalyst basket 20'8"; interchanger 84 coils of 1'7½" mean diameter, 2" O.D. pipe × 10 S.W.G.
